findings.quote: If no precipitate, water or gas forms, there is no reaction.
findings.problem: This is a false general statement about double displacement. A partner swap also goes ahead when a weak electrolyte forms, for example a weak acid: HCl(aq) + NaC2H3O2(aq) gives NaCl(aq) + HC2H3O2(aq), net ionic H+ + C2H3O2- -> HC2H3O2, with no precipitate, no water and no gas. A student using this trap would say 'no reaction' for a strong acid mixed with an acetate or fluoride salt. The base lesson taught this driving force ('formation of a precipitate, weak electrolyte/water, or gas'; 'check whether a precipitate, gas, or weak electrolyte forms'), so correct teaching was cut. The core text hedges with 'There are three common ones.', but the trap turns the three into a complete list. This sentence was already present in the round-1 text and was not raised then.
findings.source: Brown, LeMay et al., Chemistry: The Central Science, Section 4.2 (metathesis reactions proceed when an insoluble solid, a weak or nonelectrolyte, or a gas forms); base lesson 7032eec5 lines 27, 99 and 107; reader-rules.md, Added after the Sol audit; content-checklist B01
